MARKING SCHEME
BUSINESS STUDIES – GRADE 10
SECTION A: (30 MARKS)
QUESTION 1 (5 MARKS)
(a) Security features:
 • Watermark
 • Security thread / hologram / raised print (any 2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(b) Importance of money:
 • Medium of exchange / facilitates trade / measure of value (any 1 × 1 = 1 mark)
(c) Currency:
 • Legal tender used in a country for buying and selling goods and services (1 mark)
(d) Ethical practice:
 • Not counterfeiting money / honesty in transactions / not defacing currency (any 1 × 1 = 1 mark)
QUESTION 2 (5 MARKS)
(a) SMART characteristics:
 • Specific (increase sales by 20%)
 • Time-bound (3 months) (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(b) Importance of goal setting:
 • Provides direction / improves performance / enhances planning (any 1 × 1 = 1 mark)
(c) Factors considered:
 • Resources available
 • Market demand
 • Skills/ability of business owners (any 2 × 1 = 2 marks)
QUESTION 3 (5 MARKS)
(a) Types of accounts:
 • Savings account
 • Current account (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(b) Importance of banking:
 • Safe keeping of money / facilitates loans / encourages savings (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(c) Banking trend in Kenya:
 • Mobile banking / agency banking / internet banking (1 × 1 = 1 mark)
QUESTION 4 (5 MARKS)
(a) Classification:
 • Primary activity (transport/trading)
 • Secondary activity (manufacturing) (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(b) Opportunity cost:
 • The value of the next best alternative foregone (1 mark)
(c) Factors influencing business environment:
 • Government policies
 • Competition
 • Technology (any 2 × 1 = 2 marks)
QUESTION 5 (5 MARKS)
(a) Factors of production:
 • Labour
 • Capital
 • Land (3 × 1 = 3 marks)
(b) Distinction:
 • Division of labour: splitting work into tasks
 • Specialization: focus on one task or skill (2 marks)
QUESTION 6 (5 MARKS)
(a) Remedies:
 • Replacement of goods
 • Refund
 • Repair (any 2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(b) Importance of customer satisfaction:
 • Builds loyalty / increases sales / improves reputation (2 marks)
(c) Consumer protection:
 • Measures to safeguard consumers against unfair trade practices (1 mark)
SECTION B: (50 MARKS)
QUESTION 7 (10 MARKS)
(a) Advantages of cooperative society:
 • Pooling resources increases capital
 • Equal profit sharing
 • Easy access to loans
 • Democratic management
 • Encourages saving (any 3 × 2 = 6 marks)
(b) Distinction:
 • Sole proprietorship: owned by one person
 • Partnership: owned by two or more people
 • Sole bears all profits/losses alone, partnership shares (4 marks)
QUESTION 8 (10 MARKS)
(a) Entrepreneurial skills:
 • Creativity
 • Risk taking
 • Decision making
 • Leadership
 • Communication (5 × 1 = 5 marks)
(b) Sources of business ideas:
 • Market gaps
 • Personal experience
 • Media/internet (any 3 × 1 = 3 marks)
(c) Benefits of incubation:
 • Business support services
 • Training and mentorship (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
QUESTION 9 (10 MARKS)
(a) Total cost:
5000 + 3000 + 1000 = Ksh 9,000 (2 marks)
(b) Fixed vs variable costs:
 • Fixed costs: constant regardless of output
 • Variable costs: change with output (4 marks)
(c) Roles of producer:
 • Produces goods/services
 • Employs labour
 • Creates employment
 • Supplies goods to consumers (any 2 × 2 = 4 marks)
QUESTION 10 (10 MARKS)
(a) Source documents:
 • Invoice
 • Receipt
 • Debit note
 • Credit note
 • Cheque (any 4 × 1 = 4 marks)
(b) Importance of books of original entry:
 • Provide evidence of transactions
 • Help in recording daily transactions
 • Basis for financial statements
 • Prevent fraud/errors (any 3 × 2 = 6 marks)
QUESTION 11 (10 MARKS)
(a) Importance of taxation:
 • Source of government revenue
 • Funding public services
 • Promotes economic development
 • Redistributes income (any 3 × 2 = 6 marks)
(b) Ethical issues:
 • Tax evasion
 • Corruption / bribery (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
(c) Customs duties:
 • Import duty
 • Export duty (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
QUESTION 12 (10 MARKS)
(a) Benefits of international trade:
 • Earn foreign exchange
 • Availability of goods
 • Encourages specialization
 • Promotes economic growth
 • Market expansion (any 4 × 2 = 8 marks)
(b) Limitations:
 • Trade restrictions
 • Dependence on other countries (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
QUESTION 13 (10 MARKS)
(a) Features of product label:
 • Product name
 • Expiry date
 • Manufacturer details
 • Brand/logo (4 × 1 = 4 marks)
(b) Importance of labeling:
 • Identifies product
 • Provides information
 • Attracts customers
 • Ensures safety (any 2 × 2 = 4 marks)
(c) Safety measures:
 • Use protective gear
 • Proper handling of machines (2 × 1 = 2 marks)
